notes.decision: Treated the overlined ⲉ̄ at line start as a section/marginal numeral (5) preserved within the body; left as parenthetical '(5)' in English. Could alternatively be a textual marker.
Greek-derived participle from χαλάω 'loosen, slack'; rendered 'slackened.' Could alternatively be a corruption. Confidence low.

Plural noun of unclear etymology. Tentatively rendered 'bewildered ones' from context (those among whom the slackened soul exists). Could relate to ⲡⲱⲱϩⲥ̄ 'distress' or be a Greek loan. Flag for parallels.

Translated 'beautiful fragrance.' Lyc. ϣⲙ̄ⲛⲟⲩϩⲉ likely orthographic variant of ϣⲙⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ 'fragrance, incense' (Sah. with ϥ; Lyc. with ϩ via dialectal alternation). Fits the liturgical greeting series: peace + kiss + fragrance.

Greek πύργος 'tower' with diminutive πυργίσκος, or with adjectival/extended ending. Translated 'the tower' / 'the towered one'; cosmological referent (likely the cosmic tower or watchtower of the soul-gathering apparatus).

Parsed as ⲁ-ⲡ-ⲟⲩⲱⲍⲙⲉ 'to the answering' — Lyc. ⲟⲩⲱⲍⲙⲉ = nominalization of ⲟⲩⲱϣⲃ 'answer, respond' (cf. ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ 'the Answer' in vocab). The faculties stand at their place 'for the answering' in the icon of the Father — the cosmic call/answer pattern.

Read ⲡ̄ as abbreviation/sigil for ⲣ̄- 'do, make' (verbal prefix). Construction: ⲁ ⲡⲡⲛⲁ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̂ ⲣ̄ ⲥⲁϣϩ ⲛⲍⲱⲃ = 'the Living Spirit performed seven works.' This matches the chapter title and the subsequent enumeration.

'The one who was clothed and crucified' — the Manichaean Jesus patibilis, the suffering Jesus stretched out across all matter and bound in every body. The Living Spirit's second work is to spread this suffering Jesus throughout the cosmos. ⲡⲉⲧⲁϩⲃⲱϭⲥ parsed as relative perfect 'who has been clothed' (passive sense of ⲃⲱϭⲥ 'cover, clothe').

Tricolon of cosmic defeat: 'struck down, spread out, crucified the substances of death.' Restored [ⲍ]ⲱⲙ as ⲍⲱⲙ = ϩⲱⲙ 'beat, strike down' (Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ). The three verbs progressively bind the dark substances to the cosmic structure.
Compound ⲙⲁⲛ- ('place of') + ⲭⲗⲟⲡⲉ ('deceit, secret thing,' Lyc. for ϭⲗⲟⲡⲉ). 'Places of deceit' — cosmological loci of cosmic falsehood that the three living words are set against.

Truncated; likely the start of ⲡⲡⲓⲗⲁⲥⲙⲁ/ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲙⲁ 'the molding' (Greek loanword for the dark fashioning, cf. ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲙⲁ in vocab). The three words fight against the three places of deceit, and other words against the molding.

Relative perfect 'who found him' — masculine object suffix ϩ (Lyc. for ϥ). Subject from prior context (likely the Father or one of the apostolic emissaries finding the soul-emissary in the Virgin of Light).
Abstract noun ⲙⲛ̄ⲧ-ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'state-of-being' (Lyc. ⲭ for ϣ) with possessive ⲧⲉϩ- 'his.' Renders the Living Spirit's 'existence' or 'cosmic career' during which he performed seven works.
